newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - PacifiCare issues Q2 outlook.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - PacifiCare issues Q2 outlook.

text.p: PacifiCare Health Systems Inc Friday said results for the quarter ending June 30, 1997 are expected to be sharply below the year ago quarter and analysts expectations.
The following is the company's news release.

CYPRESS, Calif., June 27 - PacifiCare Health Systems, Inc. (Nasdaq: PHSYA and PHSYB) said today that financial results for the quarter ending June 30, 1997 are expected to be in the range of $0.30 to $0.45 per share, compared to $1.15 per share before pre-tax charges for the same period last year. The expected financial results are lower than analysts' estimates for the quarter which, on June 20, 1997, averaged $1.16 per share. The reduction in expected earnings is based on information currently available for April and a preliminary analysis of May.

The Company said the primary reason for the expected earnings shortfall is substantially higher health care costs in its commercial and Medicare lines of business in a number of its markets, mainly those recently acquired in the FHP International Corporation transaction, but also in PacifiCare's California and Oregon markets. Also impacting the quarter's results are a number of non- recurring expenses, primarily in its California operations, resulting from reserve increases which are routinely re-estimated, retroactive adjustments and a write-off associated with a computer system conversion. Additionally, the effective tax rate is expected to be substantially higher as a result of non-deductible goodwill amortization.

By comparison to the higher than expected health care costs, quarter-to- date revenue and membership results continue to run in line with the Company's expectations. Additionally, marketing, general and administrative costs, which include expenses related to the integration of FHP, are performing better than expected.
State-specific issues impacting the expected financial results include:

Utah. The Utah market is performing below expectations due to a shift of membership from capitated to non-capitated portions of its health care provider network, resulting in higher health care costs. Additionally, commercial product pricing has been determined to be lower than necessary to cover actual costs. The Company believes that the difficulties in Utah, a former FHP market, comprise approximately one-fourth of the overall expected shortfall. Management has already begun raising prices in the Utah market and has already implemented a recontracting process that is expected to result in more cost-effective provider relationships.

FHP California. The FHP California market is performing below expectations as a result of a decline in commercial prices in late 1996 that have resulted in higher health care costs as a percentage of premium revenue (the medical loss ratio). The Company believes that the difficulties in the FHP California market comprise approximately one-fourth of the overall expected shortfall. Management has already begun establishing price increases in FHP's products, which are expected to have an adverse effect on overall membership growth. Additionally, the Company has already begun recontracting with FHP's providers, although the successful renegotiation of these contracts will be, in part, dependent upon the California Department of Corporations' timely approval of the combination of the PacifiCare and FHP health plan licenses in that state. Management reiterated its belief that it continues to benefit from the cost-savings realized from the timely integration of the two California operations.

Nevada. The Nevada market's difficulties are primarily caused by previous administrative changes in the claims processing area which resulted in reduced visibility of projected claims costs when compared to actual claims costs. This impacted both contracting and pricing decisions made in late 1996 to early 1997. Additionally, commercial product pricing in a number of rural areas has been determined to be lower than necessary to cover actual costs. The Company believes that the difficulties in Nevada, a former FHP market, comprise approximately ten percent of the overall expected shortfall. Management has already implemented corrective action by relocating the Nevada claims processing function to Arizona from Colorado and establishing better management oversight and controls. Improved provider contracts have been signed and efforts are underway to move most of its members into capitated portions of the provider network. Management will also begin raising prices to more accurately reflect actual costs and work to establish closer relationships with contracting providers to implement more cost-effective contracts.

FHP Texas. The challenges in the FHP Texas market are the result of recent start-up efforts in both the commercial and Medicare lines of business. Management expects to complete the integration of the FHP Texas operations into its own Texas operations by July 1, 1997. These efforts, combined with a provider recontracting effort, are expected to significantly reduce the operating losses currently being incurred.

PacifiCare California. The results in the PacifiCare California market continue to be impacted by higher than expected prescription drug costs and higher health care costs in its Medicare program. Management is continuing to develop ways to minimize the impact of prescription drug costs on its operations. The success in controlling these costs is, in part, influenced by certain arrangements between the Company and the California Department of Corporations as part of the FHP acquisition that generally are designed to minimize changes in both providers and formulary.

Oregon. The Oregon market is continuing to experience a higher than expected medical loss ratio due to expansion efforts into the southern part of that state and the recent addition of new commercial products that are not yet profitable. Management has implemented price increases to more accurately reflect actual costs and has initiated provider recontracting efforts. If unsuccessful, management expects to exit unprofitable areas and product lines.

The Company stated that for the twelve months ending December 31, 1997 it expects a significantly lower membership growth rate in both its commercial and Medicare product lines compared to last year. The total medical loss ratio is also expected to be higher this year compared to the same period last year. Marketing, general and administrative costs as a percentage of operating revenue are expected to continue to be favorable compared to the prior year. The overall impact of these items, combined with goodwill amortization and debt costs associated with the FHP acquisition, is expected to result in a substantial decrease in the earnings for the twelve months ending December 31, 1997 compared to the same period a year ago.

"We are obviously disappointed by the performance of a number of these newly acquired assets," said Alan Hoops, president and chief executive officer. "Through this challenging time, I want to assure our members, employer customers and contracting health care providers that PacifiCare will continue to offer the same levels of quality and service that it has historically been known for.
"The integration of our two companies continues to proceed on schedule and according to our plans," Hoops continued. "Each week, we are seeing tangible results of our integration efforts.

"I believe the combination of PacifiCare and FHP has created a position of strength from which to attack these challenges," concluded Hoops. "I am as confident as ever that our dedicated employees will help PacifiCare work through these issues and that we will continue to be successful."

PacifiCare Health Systems is one of the nation's leading managed health care services companies. Primary operations include managed care products for employer groups, and Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries in 14 states and Guam serving nearly four million members. Other specialty managed care operations include life and health insurance, behavioral health services, workers' compensation, dental and vision services, pharmacy benefit management and Medicare risk management services.
Cautionary Statement:

The statements contained in this release that are not historical facts are forward looking statements that are based on management's estimates, assumptions and projections. Important factors that could cause results to differ materially from those expected by management include an unexpected increase in competition, an unfavorable pricing environment, the inability to achieve expected efficiencies in operations or effectively control health care costs, the inability to successfully integrate the FHP acquisition and the possibility of regulatory delays relating to the integration of the two companies. Additional information on factors that could potentially affect the Company's financial results may be found in documents filed by the Company with the Securities and Exchange Commission. SOURCE PacifiCare Health Systems, Inc.
